newsitem.title: UK: Life director to leave UK insurance body.
newsitem.headline: Life director to leave UK insurance body.

text.p: Paul Smee is to leave the Association of British Insurers, where he heads the life insurance division, to take up a post at the Independent Television Commission at the end of October.
An ABI spokesman told Reuters on Friday that Smee had been headhunted by the ITC. He said a report in the Guardian newspaper that Smee was leaving because of problems within the industry was untrue.
The newspaper said insurers faced problems in drawing up a plan to transfer responsibility for pensions, long term care and health insurance provision to individuals from the state.
"There is no split. He is leaving the ABI because he was made a better offer," the spokesman said.
"We're talking to our members, but there's no sort of difficulty in terms of widespread problems which have led to his moving on from the ABI."
"We're looking at the whole issue of the transfer of welfare responsibilities, which is so wide-ranging that we have to look at all possibilities," he said.
The ABI is looking for a successor to Smee and hopes to appoint someone shortly, the spokesman added.
